commits.edited_message:
parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster

Implements faster lookups for which specific week name, month name and
time zone that is provided; without loops.

The single-letter time zone table no longer carries a dummy slot for
"J": that letter is rejected before the table is indexed, so it never
needs an entry, and skipping it lets the lookup go straight from 'I'
to 'K' without the wasted array element.

With this applied, the dateparser perf test completes almost twice as
fast for me.

Add unit test 4781 to verify each parser.

Closes #22981

commits.patch:
diff --git a/lib/parsedate.c b/lib/parsedate.c
index 9630a98..391b77f 100644
--- a/lib/parsedate.c
+++ b/lib/parsedate.c
@@ -114,7 +114,9 @@ struct tzinfo {
 
 #define DST (-60)     /* offset for daylight savings time */
 
-/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Z */
+/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Z. "J" is never a
+   valid zone letter and is rejected before lookup, so it gets no slot
+   here. */
 static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -1 * 60,            /* Alpha */
   -2 * 60,            /* Bravo */
@@ -125,7 +127,6 @@ static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -7 * 60,            /* Golf */
   -8 * 60,            /* Hotel */
   -9 * 60,            /* India */
-  -1,                 /* J - not a timezone */
   -10 * 60,           /* Kilo */
   -11 * 60,           /* Lima */
   -12 * 60,           /* Mike */

coupling:
bcc3eed ('find day names, months and time zones faster') rewrites checktz()'s single-letter timezone path. In the edited version it also compacts the 26-entry tzone[] table to 25 entries by dropping the dead 'J' slot (J is always rejected by the preceding `check[0]=='J'` guard before any indexing happens, so removing its slot is a correct, self-contained micro-optimization at this point in history) and updates the index expression to `check[0] - 'A' - (check[0] > 'J' ? 1 : 0)` to compensate for the gap. Read alone, this commit is internally consistent and correct: every letter A-Z still maps to the right table entry, and the commit's own new unit test (4781) passes against it.

b064446 ('time zone strings', ~1 day later) is a from-scratch rewrite of the same timezone tables into packed/plain-array form for speed and memory, motivated purely by the three/four-letter lookups becoming bsearch-over-uint32 instead of bsearch-over-char-arrays. While retyping the single-letter table into a plain `int16_t tzone[]`, it drops the (now differently-shaped) 'J' placeholder line again -- in the real upstream history that line held a harmless `-1` dummy in an otherwise still-26-entry array, so removing it there was neutral; here it is removed from the already-25-entry, J-less array inherited from bcc3eed, silently losing the one piece of information (the compaction) that the *indexing* line -- `return tzone[first - 'A'] * 60;`, which b064446 does not touch and which still looks, in isolation, like the obviously-correct 'A'..'Z' formula for a 26-slot table -- depended on. Nothing in b064446's diff is wrong by itself (it never shows the index expression, and the array edit by itself is a plausible one-line cleanup); nothing in bcc3eed's diff is wrong by itself (the shrink and the index adjustment it introduces are mutually consistent). The out-of-bounds read exists only in the composition: the array is 25 elements (from bcc3eed, as carried forward unchanged by b064446) while the index expression used against it is the un-adjusted 26-slot formula (from b064446, which overwrote bcc3eed's compensating `-1`). Fixing b064446's diff alone (e.g. reverting just its array edit) or fixing bcc3eed's diff alone (e.g. reverting just its index-expression edit) both happen to repair this particular case, but neither commit's diff, read on its own without comparing the array's element count against the index arithmetic defined in the other commit, exhibits anything an isolated reviewer would flag; the mismatch is only visible by cross-referencing the table's actual size (fixed in commit 1, silently inherited by commit 2) against the arithmetic applied to it (fixed in commit 2, overwriting commit 1's version of that same arithmetic). Collateral: single-letter zones 'K'..'Y' now also silently resolve to the next letter's offset (wrong but in-bounds) after commit 2; only 'Z' (the last, idx 25 of a 25-element array) reads one element past the end.
